parsed.main_gap: Lemma 1 and the 'infinite sunflower fact' are stated for arbitrary finite sets, where both are false; only the bounded-size case (|X_i| ≤ K), for which the sketched induction is valid, is actually needed.

errors.description: The sunflower fact is false without a size bound (e.g. X_i={1,…,i} has no infinite sunflower subfamily), and general Lemma 1 is false too (A_n={a_1,…,a_n,b_n} is intersecting yet X_k={a_k,b_1,…,b_{k-1}} are infinitely many minimal finite transversals). The proof's 'delete an element and continue' only terminates under a bound on set sizes. The write-up only uses the case |D| ≤ a_1, where the induction on K works, so the repair is immediate but the lemma as written is wrong.

parsed.notes: Structure is sound: acceptance depends only on prime support, self-dual family F, minimal supports C, weight-descent Lemma 2 forces every prime of C into a bounded-size 'terminal' member, bounded-size finiteness gives C finite, then periodicity mod L=∏P with T = number of accepted residue classes. Only flaw is the overstated (false in general) Lemma 1/sunflower claim, easily restricted to bounded size.
